az_paradox_rock.blurb: Paradox Rock is a small crag near the top of Bear Canyon on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson. Nine single-day-sized routes mix bolted lines with a few gear climbs, running from easy fifth class into the low 5.12 range, with most of the grades clustered in the 5.9 to 5.11 band. The stone is described as good quality, with slabby faces, cracks and some overhanging sections. The wall catches plenty of sun, so it stays pleasant on winter days. It is an easy place to fill a day for leaders working in the middle grades, and it sees little traffic.

az_tombstone_area.blurb: Tombstone Area is a bouldering pocket on the Mount Elden side of Flagstaff, within Gloria's, a maze of boulders and low cliffs set among ponderosa pines. It sits a few minutes west of the Heart Cave, near where the boulder field thins out. Nine problems range from V1 up through V4, with a V7 classic and a pair of V9 lines for strong climbers. The rock is dacite, which is rough on skin and climbs thin and technical. A tall block offers several good lines, and the cliffs above attract highball and top-rope attention. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons.

az_brush_monkey_boulders.blurb: Brush Monkey Boulders is a small bouldering spot off Copper Basin Road west of Prescott, tucked into brush on a slope that faces west. Only a handful of boulders are scattered here, but they offer good stone and wide views. The nine problems stretch from an easy V0 crack warm-up through the V3 and V4 range, then up to a few hard lines near V6 to V8. The first boulder is a good place to loosen up before dropping to the main group. Expect a short, brushy walk in, and expect it to feel quiet and low-key.

az_atlantis_1.blurb: Atlantis #1 is a small bouldering area at Oak Flat in Queen Creek Canyon, east of Phoenix near Superior. Rounded, freestanding boulders sit in a wash between two neighboring sections, including one large block with a little cave at its west end. The nine problems fall in a narrow band, mostly V2 and V3 with a single V4, so it suits climbers working through the middle grades. The stone around Oak Flat is abrasive, with a wide variety of hold types, and the walk from the nearby sectors takes only a minute or two.

az_hidden_jewels.blurb: Hidden Jewels is a small single-pitch crag low on the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, above Tucson. Nine climbs, mostly gear routes with a couple of bolted lines, run from about 5.4 to 5.10-, with many sitting in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. The wall faces west, so it gets morning shade and afternoon sun, and its low elevation keeps it warm when higher crags are cold. The rock is dustier and more broken than at many neighbors, and most climbs need some gear beyond their bolts. A single day covers everything, and the walk up through saguaros is steep.

az_karma_cave.blurb: Karma Cave is one of the sport sections at the Homestead, a limestone canyon in central Arizona between Globe and Winkelman. Nine routes run from 5.9 into the 5.13 range, and most sit around 5.11. The climbing is steep and bouldery near the ground, easing into shorter face moves higher up, so it favors people who are comfortable on powerful starts. The cave gets shade in the morning. Reaching it means following the creekbed past a neighboring wall, then going up a gully and along the base of a cliff.

az_lost_whiskey_wall.blurb: Lost Whiskey Wall is a bouldering wall in the Lower Canyon of Saguaro Lake, east of Phoenix, on the south side as you head up the channel. It is reached by water rather than by a trail. Nine easy problems, from the very easiest up to V2, cover slabs, faces, a roof, a corner and a crack, with many variations between them. Most climbers find it the simplest of the lake's crags to get to. It is sunny early and shaded later, so mornings and evenings are the best times to visit.
